analysis.summary: Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by Rockingham County for the construction of a Utility Office. The procurement is governed by the Virginia Public Procurement Act. Contact person is Trish Davidson, Deputy County Administrator. The provided procurement tender document outlines the table of contents and sections covering purpose, background, scope of services, proposal preparation, evaluation and award criteria, general terms and conditions, and various administrative and legal clauses. The County of Rockingham, Virginia is seeking design-build proposals from pre-qualified firms (Harman Construction and Legacy Building Company) for the construction of a new Utility Office and garage bay extensions located at 955 Pleasant Valley Road, Harrisonburg, Virginia. The RFP (Request for Proposal) is for the County of Rockingham to construct a utility building. Offerors must submit a detailed proposal including project design, company history, compliance with the RFP's purpose and scope, and a total cost with cost breakdowns. Proposals must be submitted by June 27, 2025, at 2:00 PM. The provided text outlines the evaluation criteria, interview schedule, and award process for a county procurement project, including weighted scoring factors and negotiation procedures. The RFP process for a project is outlined, with key dates including RFP issuance (April 11, 2025), pre-proposal meeting (April 28, 2025), proposal cutoff (June 27, 2025), evaluation period (June 30 – July 2, 2025), interviews (July 3rd), RFP decision (July 16, 2025), Board of Supervisors consideration (July 23, 2025), and construction completion (December 31, 2025). The solicitation includes general terms and conditions, focusing on applicable laws (Commonwealth of Virginia), anti-discrimination (Federal Civil Rights Act, Virginia Fair Employment Contracting Act, Virginians With Disabilities Act, Americans With Disabilities Act, and § 2.2-4311 of the Virginia Public Procurement Act (VPPA)). The provided procurement text outlines standard terms and conditions for public contracting with Rockingham County, including subcontracting clauses, ethics and anti-collusion certifications, compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act, antitrust assignments, clarification procedures, progress payment terms, and vendor qualification investigations. The County outlines its rights regarding inspection, changes to the contract, defaults, and tax exemptions for this procurement. Section 7.13 outlines the mandatory insurance requirements for the awarded offeror, including statutory Workers' Compensation, Employer's Liability, Commercial General Liability, Automobile Liability, Umbrella Liability Coverage, and Professional (E&O) Liability Insurance, along with specific endorsement and waiver of subrogation requirements naming the County of Rockingham. This document outlines the insurance requirements for a County contract, including carrier ratings, policy types, additional insured endorsements, proof of insurance submission before performance, subcontractor coverage obligations, and waivers of subrogation. The County of Rockingham specifies insurance requirements for contractors, including umbrella/excess liability, professional liability, builder's risk, and notification requirements. The County retains the right to revise or reject insurance requirements. This document outlines terms and conditions for a county contract including insurance requirements, drug-free workplace obligations, nondiscrimination, audit rights, non-appropriation, and contract document definitions. The procurement text outlines rules regarding contract interpretation, compliance with Virginia laws and regulations, licensing/permitting requirements, and proposal submission procedures. This procurement text covers proposal receipt deadlines, confidentiality, proposal acceptance periods, termination by the county, and legal protections for proprietary information. This document outlines compliance requirements for bidders submitting proposals in response to a Request for Proposal (RFP). Requirements include debarment certification, bonding (labor & material payment and performance), and a signature sheet certifying compliance and prohibiting collusion. Additional information includes notification deadlines for bond execution.

requirements.description: Proper Proposal Submission.

evidence.excerpt: Proposals must give the full business address of the Offeror and be signed by an agent authorized to bind the Offeror. Proposals by partnerships must furnish the full name of all partners and must be signed in the partnership name by one of the general partners or any authorized representative, followed by the designation of the person signing. Proposals by corporations must be signed with the legal name of the corporation followed by the name of the State in which it is incorporated and by the signature and designation of the president, secretary, or other person authorized to bind it in the matter. The name of each person signing shall also be typed or printed below the signature. A proposal by a person who affixes to the signature the word “ President, ” “ Secretary, ” “ Agent ” or other designation without disclosing the principal, may be held to be the proposal of the individual signing. When requested by the County, satisfactory evidence of the authority of the officer signing in behalf of the corporation shall be furnished.
